note: Machine-readable design standards. Agents read this before writing any HTML. Single source of truth for palette, forbidden patterns, component HTML, and template pipeline.

logo.note: Always inline SVG wordmark — no text/CSS logo, no tag

forbidden.rule: Headers must be white with 3px brand border-bottom
Body background must be #fff, never gray
Section numbers are plain colored text, no filled circles
Sections use flat border-bottom separators, not card wrappers
Only the 11 standard palette vars allowed

No arbitrary hex colors — use CSS variables from shared-base.css.html. The exceptions list below holds semantically anchored colors used by standard components (status badges, P0 / scope / phase indicators, rail surfaces).
forbidden.legacyMigrationNote: The colors in legacyDoNotUse are present in legacy HTML files (architect portal, pitch kit, older client portals). They are blessed in `exceptions` so the lint hook stays green, but should be migrated to palette vars (var(--border), var(--mid), var(--light)) the next time each file is touched. Once a value has zero occurrences in the repo, remove it from both lists.

forbidden.rule: No external CSS frameworks — all files must be self-contained
No external font imports — system font stack only
Never use a text or CSS logo — always the inline SVG wordmark
No dark-background metric cards — use .stat-row/.stat (white bg, brand border-top)
Intake forms save to Firestore only — no mailto: in form submit
Never hardcode contact emails in templates — read architectEmail from project.json

collapsibleSection.css: details.section-block { border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border) } summary.section-head { display:flex; align-items:center; gap:12px; cursor:pointer; padding:14px 40px; list-style:none } .section-eyebrow { font-size:10px; font-weight:700; letter-spacing:2px; text-transform:uppercase; color:var(--brand) } .section-title { font-size:16px; font-weight:700; color:var(--dark) } .section-chevron { font-size:11px; color:var(--mid); transition:transform 0.2s } details.section-block[open] .section-chevron { transform:rotate(180deg) } .section-body { padding:4px 40px 24px }
rules: Key sections default open: Challenge, Solution, Flows, Investment, Next Steps
Secondary sections default collapsed: Journey, Outcomes, Timeline, Included, OOS, Assumptions
Conditional sections (ROI, About) emitted by fill-template.js when data present

phaseChip.usage: Compact chip next to a panel title showing the current AI-journey phase.

Strip any 'Phase N — ' prefix in the source label before rendering.

docHeaderMeta.usage: Intake / proposal document header. 2-column grid: title (eyebrow + h1 + subtitle) on the left, provenance meta (Prepared by, Date, Source) on the right, baseline-aligned.

rules: Right column right-aligned, baseline-anchored to H1.
<900px viewport: meta drops below title with a top border, left-aligned.
Source value should hyperlink to storage when project.json.sourceFilesFolder is set — use .source-link styling.

sourceLink.usage: Hyperlink in the Source meta row pointing at the GCS Console folder for the client's scoping files.
sourceLink.html: {sourceText} ↗

Hover lifts to var(--brand).
Render plain text (no <a>) when no sourceUrl is available.

categoryTabs.usage: Intake form — sticky pinned navigation at the top of the main column. Replaces inline category dividers. Each tab maps to a hidden anchor (#cat-{key}) immediately preceding the first section block in that bucket.
categoryTabs.css: .cat-tabs { position:sticky; top:44px; z-index:150; background:#fff; border-bottom:2px solid var(--brand); display:flex; margin:20px -24px 0; padding:0 24px } .cat-tab { flex:1; background:none; border:none; cursor:pointer; padding:10px 18px 9px; text-align:left; border-bottom:3px solid transparent; margin-bottom:-2px } .cat-tab.is-active { border-bottom-color:var(--brand); background:var(--light) }
rules: Sticky at top:44px so it sits directly below .sticky-bar (which is ~44px tall).
Click → smooth-scroll to #cat-{key} + auto-open the first section in the bucket.
Active tab state driven by IntersectionObserver on details.section-block[data-cat].
Hidden in print (covered by .no-print + @media print rule).
Future-bucket tabs use amber tinting to signal 'not in current scope'.

categoryAnchor.usage: Hidden in-document anchor that a category tab scrolls to. Sits immediately before each category's first section block.
rules: display:block; height:0; scroll-margin-top:112px;
aria-hidden so screen readers skip it.

intakeRail.usage: Sticky right column on the intake form (and any similar long form). Holds Progress, Subsections jump-nav, Needs Attention, and Links cards. Hidden in print; collapses to below content at <1100px viewport.
intakeRail.html:
...
...subsection nav...
...
...links...
rules: 260px column inside a 1480px max-width grid.
position:sticky; top:56px; max-height:calc(100vh - 72px); overflow-y:auto.
Collapses below main content at ≤1100px viewport.

railProgress.usage: Progress card at the top of intakeRail. Shows answered/total + percentage + brand-red fill bar.
railProgress.html:
Progress
0 / 0

rules: Border-left 3px brand.
Progress fill animated with width transition.
Source values mirror the .sticky-bar's #answered-count / #total-count.

railNav.usage: Subsection jump-nav grouped by category. IntersectionObserver highlights the active section in red as the user scrolls.
railNav.html:
Business
§1 Use Cases
rules: Categories appear as small uppercase labels with thin top borders.
Each anchor shows live filled/total count after JS updates.
.is-active = brand-red left border + light bg. .is-complete = green count. .has-required = red count + bold.

railAttention.usage: Needs Attention card. Pre-seeded with P0 blockers (one per <li data-target>). Dynamic 'N required unanswered' item appended by rebuildAttention() on every input.
railAttention.html:
Needs Attention
  • P0 Title Multi-sentence action body, wraps freely.
Nothing flagged. Good to go.
rules: Title and body are TWO distinct elements: .attn-title (uppercase, 11px, dark-red) on its own line; .attn-body (12px, regular, line-height 1.5) wraps freely below — never single-line clamped.
Strip leading separator characters (' — ', ': ', '· ') from clientAction text — they're historical inline separators that look orphaned now that title is display:block.
Each li[data-target] is clickable + keyboard-focusable; right-arrow ::after marker.

data-target values: 'biz' → expand .biz-context. 'sec:<id>' → open the section AND jumpToFirstUnanswered() inside it. 'first-unanswered' → scroll to the first required-empty field anywhere on the form.
Empty state surfaces when no static blockers AND no required-empty answers.

unansweredHighlight.usage: Eye-catcher applied to every .q block whose required textarea/input is empty. JS toggles .is-unanswered on every input event. Provides instant visual scan target on long forms.
unansweredHighlight.css: .q.is-unanswered { background:var(--light); border-left:3px solid var(--brand); border-radius:0 4px 4px 0; padding:6px 8px } .q.is-unanswered .q-num { color:var(--brand); font-weight:800 } .q.is-unanswered .q-num::after { content:'●'; animation:ds-pulse 1.4s ease-in-out infinite }
rules: Highlight automatically clears once the field has non-empty value (.toggle in updateProgress()).
Pulsing dot is the eye-catcher — use the @keyframes ds-pulse animation.
Honour prefers-reduced-motion: animation disabled when set.
Color signal must be brand red — no other accent.

jumpToFirstUnanswered.usage: Helper that walks required-but-empty fields in a given scope and scroll-focuses the first one. Wired into Expand-all, every rail-nav link click, every category-tab click, and the dynamic 'N required unanswered' attention item.
jumpToFirstUnanswered.rule: When a user expands or navigates anywhere on the form, the form must land on the next outstanding action rather than the top of a huge expanded block. If nothing is outstanding in the scope, fall back to the section/category header.
behavior: Expand-all → expand everything → jump to first unanswered anywhere.
Collapse-all → collapse everything → do nothing else.
Rail-nav link click → open the section → jump to first unanswered in section; if all answered, scroll to section header.
Category-tab click → open every section in the bucket → jump to first unanswered across the bucket; if all answered, scroll to bucket anchor.
Attention-list 'N unanswered' item → jump straight to first unanswered.
After scroll completes (~350ms), focus the field so keyboard input lands there immediately.

railLinks.usage: External links card. Intake-default: Your Client Portal + DS Pricing Model. Never includes the Architect Guide (internal). Meta.links[] is appended after defaults.
rules: All links open in new tab with rel=noopener.
Trailing ↗ glyph via ::after.
NEVER include internal-only docs (Architect Guide, Pitch Kit, Knowledge Base) in client-facing intake.

barTools.usage: Expand-all / Collapse-all button pair on the left of the .sticky-bar. Improves navigability when the form has many sections.
rules: Sits between .bar-logo and .progress-pill with a left divider.
Hover lifts to brand color + light bg.
Hidden in print via .sticky-bar { display:none } parent rule.

softLockBanner.usage: Intake submit confirmation banner. After every submit, shows 'v{N} submitted on {date}. You can keep editing — your next save will be v{N+1}.' Persists across reloads via localStorage on the same browser.
softLockBanner.html: ✓ v{N} submitted on {date}. You can keep editing — your next save will be v{N+1}.
rules: Versioning is the data model: every submit appends a snapshot to intake_responses/{client}.versions[] via Firestore arrayUnion.
Top-level answers/completionPct/submittedAt mirror the LATEST snapshot for backward-compatible portal reads.
localStorage key 'intake_version_{slug}' tracks best-effort per-browser version count for the banner UX.
Submit button is NEVER disabled — client can always update.

printAllExpanded.usage: Wrapper for window.print() on the intake form. Force-opens every <details> + biz-context panel BEFORE printing, then restores prior state on the afterprint event.
printAllExpanded.rule: <details> bodies are hidden by user-agent CSS when [open] is absent; @media print can't override that with display rules alone. JS must add the [open] attribute before printing.

rules: All collapsible section bodies must show in print regardless of open state
Sticky bar hidden in print
No-print sections (.no-print) hidden in print

knowledge-base.note: Generated from live JSON/YAML/MD sources at deploy time. Uses the 3-column-docs-shell pattern — the standard for all internal knowledge pages.

3-column-docs-shell.usage: All internal knowledge/reference pages. Use this pattern — never invent a new layout for internal docs.
3-column-docs-shell.description: Sticky top bar + 3-column grid: left nav (200px, sticky, section jumplinks), main content (flex: 1fr), right nav (180px, sticky, subsection links auto-built by JS scroll-spy).
3-column-docs-shell.gridCss: .docs-shell { display:grid; grid-template-columns:200px 1fr 180px; min-height:calc(100vh - 44px); max-width:1440px; margin:0 auto; }
3-column-docs-shell.topBarCss: .top-bar { position:sticky; top:0; z-index:200; background:#fff; border-bottom:2px solid var(--brand); display:flex; align-items:center; gap:14px; padding:0 20px; height:44px; }
3-column-docs-shell.navLeftCss: .nav-left { position:sticky; top:44px; height:calc(100vh - 44px); overflow-y:auto; border-right:1px solid var(--border); padding:14px 0 24px; }
3-column-docs-shell.navRightCss: .nav-right { position:sticky; top:44px; height:calc(100vh - 44px); overflow-y:auto; border-left:1px solid var(--border); padding:14px 0 24px; }
3-column-docs-shell.headingAnchors: h2 = left-nav sections (scroll-margin-top:52px), h3 = right-nav subsections (auto-built by JS)
3-column-docs-shell.scrollSpy: JS reads all h2/h3 from #docContent, builds both navs, updates active states on scroll
rules: Left nav links to h2 sections only — one per section
Right nav is built by JS scroll-spy from h3s within the active h2 section
Top bar is sticky at 44px height, white background, brand red bottom border
Body background is #fff — never gray or dark
Responsive: right nav hides at 1100px, left nav goes static at 720px

accessRules.internal: Firebase Google auth required, restricted to @dataskate.ai
accessRules.external: Publicly accessible — share via direct link or embed in client portal

dateFormat.note: All user-visible dates across portals, proposals, and intake forms must use this format. ISO dates from JSON/storage must be converted at render time.
